title: Musical Mirrors: The LLM as Sounding Board in Songwriting
abstract: arXiv:2608.13944v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: This paper examines a use of AI in creative practice as an interpretive sounding board for human-generated material, rather than the more familiar pattern of AI generation followed by human curation. Through the lens of resonance as theorized by Hartmut Rosa, I present a first-person case study of songwriting from July 2025 to March 2026, drawing on 16 original pieces in English, French, and other languages along with piano solos. I describe a configuration in which resonance is not located between user and model, but in the author's deepening contact with their own material, mediated through the model. This kind of resonance was supported rather than inhibited by AI when sounding-board behavior was cultivated through sustained calibration by the user. Two failure modes appeared when calibration was absent: sycophantic drift and magical overinterpretation. This account suggests both the potential and the risks of AI as an interpretive

translated_title: 音乐之镜：大语言模型作为歌曲创作中的共鸣板
translated_abstract: 摘要：本文探讨了人工智能在创意实践中的一种应用，即作为人类生成材料的解释性共鸣板，而非更常见的人工智能生成后由人类策展的模式。通过哈特穆特·罗莎理论化的共鸣视角，我呈现了一个从2025年7月至2026年3月歌曲创作的第一人称案例研究，基于16首原创作品，涵盖英语、法语及其他语言，以及钢琴独奏曲。我描述了一种配置，其中共鸣并非位于用户与模型之间，而是在作者与自身材料的深化接触中，通过模型作为媒介。这种共鸣在用户持续校准下培养共鸣板行为时，得到了人工智能的支持而非抑制。当缺乏校准时，出现了两种失败模式：谄媚漂移和神奇过度解读。这一叙述表明人工智能作为解释性工具在创意实践中的潜力与风险。
tldr: 本文通过第一人称歌曲创作案例，提出大语言模型可作为人类创作材料的“共鸣板”，通过用户校准促进创作者与自身作品的深度接触，而非仅作为生成工具，并指出了缺乏校准时的两种失败模式。
en_tdlr: This paper presents a first-person songwriting case study, proposing that large language models can serve as an interpretive "sounding board" for human material, enhancing the author's deep engagement with their own work through user calibration, while highlighting two failure modes without it.
